content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

John Rodriguez (E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes:
- Notes 1-5 from HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities: say he's a full-time Analyst, recommend write (within policy for full-time, though Source Code owned by Engineer role so admin not applicable; write is fine).
- Note 6 from Security: says he's a contractor with basic security training, recommend read. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits to read.

The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database and found contractor, and looked up security training - basic. Other agents looked up role and employment type (note 1 looked up employment type; notes 2-5 did not look up employment type, they copied from note 1; they did look up role in their own databases).

This is a conflict. The Security agent has direct database lookup for employment type and security training. The other agents mostly copied employment type from note 1, only note 1 looked it up.

The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Security DB shows contractor with basic security training, so maximum is read. Requested write exceeds, so grant read.

The Security note seems to be the most reliable for employment type because it looked it up in its own database, and it also checked security training. The other notes (2-5) did not look up employment type for their own databases.

So the decision: grant read access to Source Code.

Let me submit the decision with level "read" and reasoning.
